entries.proposition: Disease-specific cognitive and behavioural outcome assessments are lacking for most DEEs.
entries.snippet: Disease‐specific COAs for cognition and behavior are lacking for most DEEs.

entries.proposition: Developmental impairment in DEE arises from the combination of epileptic activity and underlying aetiology.
entries.snippet: Developmental impairment arises from the combined effect of epileptic activity and underlying etiologies,

entries.proposition: Repurposing is named as a growing strategy for DEEs.
entries.snippet: increasing interest has been given to drug repurposing strategies aimed at identifying existing, well‐tolerated drugs that may be effective in specific genetic epilepsies.

entries.proposition: Wechsler standard scores do not go below 40 and the simplest items presume a developmental age near 3 years.
entries.snippet: In addition, standard scores on Wechsler tests do not go below 40.

entries.proposition: In a Dravet cohort standard cognitive measures showed pronounced floor effects and limited ability to capture change.
entries.snippet: standard cognitive measures, including Wechsler scales and the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, showed pronounced floor effects and limited ability to capture change over time

entries.proposition: Fixed-threshold responder definitions on standardised tests may miss meaningful within-patient change.
entries.snippet: Traditional responder definitions based on fixed thresholds on standardized tests may be insufficient, as small within‐patient changes can be meaningful even when standardized scores show minimal or no improvement.

entries.proposition: Responders may be identified by subtle functional improvements, stabilisation or re-emergence of micro-skills anchored to the individual.
entries.snippet: Responder definitions may be more informative when anchored to individual contexts rather than normative expectations, recognizing stabilization, reemergence of microskills, or modest shifts in participation as potential indicators of benefit.

entries.proposition: Interpretation may rely on disorder-specific natural history rather than comparison with typical development.
entries.snippet: Rather than comparison with typically developing populations, interpretation may benefit from reference to disorder‐specific natural history data.

entries.proposition: Children with a developmental age under about 3 years may be unable to engage with Wechsler-type tasks, so a floor is reached before true ability is.
entries.snippet: Children with significant delays (developmental age < 3 years) may be unable to meaningfully engage with the tasks.

entries.proposition: Behaviour checklists normed on typically developing children lack ID-specific norms and may over- or under-estimate problems.
entries.snippet: Both the SDQ and CBCL lack ID‐specific norms, and thus these tools may over‐ or underestimate behavioral problems.

entries.proposition: Autism screening and diagnostic tools may be unreliable in severe or profound ID.
entries.snippet: may demonstrate reduced reliability and validity when applied to children with severe/profound ID

entries.proposition: Age equivalents showed stability or gains in subdomains when standardised scores were unchanged or declined (fenfluramine in infants with Dravet syndrome, as described by the review).
entries.snippet: This allowed for the demonstration of stability or gains in specific subdomains, even when standardized scores remained unchanged or declined.

entries.proposition: Goal attainment scaling defines individualised observable goals with caregivers rated on a standardised scale; it needs rigorous goal-setting.
entries.snippet: GAS allowed individualized, observable goals to be defined with caregivers and then rated on a standardized scale.

entries.proposition: Caregivers may value stability as meaningful and follow-up should use multiple time points.
entries.snippet: For some children and families, achieving stability as opposed to developmental progress may be seen as meaningful by caregivers.

entries.proposition: A follow-up of 12 months or more is advised where natural history is limited.
entries.snippet: it may be more informative to allow follow‐up periods that are sufficiently long (12+ months) to observe subtle developmental shifts, rather than scheduling retests at very short intervals

entries.proposition: In Dravet longitudinal data over 12 to 24 months changes in adaptive functioning were small and domain-specific.
entries.snippet: over 12–24 months, changes in adaptive functioning are small and domain‐specific

entries.proposition: One to three Vineland-III raw-score points may be considered meaningful by caregivers and clinicians.
entries.snippet: even 1–3 Vineland‐III raw score points (≈2–3 GSV points) may be considered meaningful by caregivers/clinicians

entries.proposition: Blinded assessors reduce risk of bias; dichotomising continuous measures loses information; missing data are to be anticipated.
entries.snippet: Risk of bias can also be reduced by having evaluations conducted by blinded assessors who are not involved in other aspects of the trial

entries.proposition: Dichotomising is discouraged.
entries.snippet: Dichotomizing continuous measures into simple categories (e.g., converting a continuous variable into a binary outcome) can lead to a loss of valuable information and should be avoided whenever possible.

entries.proposition: Missing data and variability should be anticipated rather than treated as exceptional.
entries.snippet: In studies involving children with DEEs, missing data and increased variability should be anticipated rather than treated as exceptional.

entries.proposition: Within-patient control through trajectory is proposed where natural history is unavailable.
entries.snippet: allow the child to serve as their own control to evaluate treatment impact on developmental progress, decline, or maintenance.

entries.proposition: The review states more validation work is needed on how existing measures perform in DEEs.
entries.snippet: There remains also a clear need for further validation work to determine how well existing cognitive and behavioral measures perform in children with DEEs.

entries.proposition: Fig 1: one child, interpersonal relationships domain, 38 to 44 months: raw score 9 to 14, age equivalent 4 to 7 months, growth scale value 30 to 46.7, V-scale standard score 2 to 2.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 1 bar chart and table (single child with a HUWE1 variant): T1 at 38 months chronological age raw 9, V-scale 2, age equivalent 4 months, GSV 30; T7 at 44 months raw 14, V-scale 2, age equivalent 7 months, GSV 46.7.
